legs.what: view depends on view depends on view (transitive closure, depth 3)
INSTEAD OF trigger hanging on a view that is itself kept
a CTE shadows the name of a real table outside the subset
quoted and schema-qualified references to a kept table
reference that lives inside a subquery used as an expression
the table a trigger body writes to, not the one it hangs on
partial index, expression index and collation index on a kept table
objects replay in an order the restore can follow
counters carry over with no row belonging to a table outside the subset
a tables= request the HTTP surface passes through is answered, by a file that loads or by an error, never by a broken file
identifiers written in [brackets] -- in FROM, as an index target, as the table a trigger hangs on
WITH where it is not expected: a FROM subquery, the right of IN, a scalar subquery, the head of an INSERT in a trigger body
syntax SQLite has taken since 3.39: RIGHT and FULL OUTER JOIN, IS DISTINCT FROM, IN (VALUES ...), 1_000, ORDER BY inside an aggregate, a quoted type name in CAST
a view whose table was dropped under it comes back, and still fails the way it failed before
a view naming a column that is not there comes back where the original fails the same way, and does not where it would not
a trigger that fails on the very operation it hangs on comes back, so the table goes on refusing that operation
the chain runs through an object that is already broken: a view over a view that does not answer
the subset decides for the broken view: v_badcol rides beside its table and stays out of a subset that dropped it, because 'no such table' is not the error the original gives
a subset that names no real table restores an empty database: being broken in the original is not a ticket to ride along
two tables kept and a broken view naming a third: membership in the subset, not brokenness, decides -- next to objects that do ride broken
a view whose UNION arms differ in width fails that way in the original; 'no such table' is a different answer, so it stays out of the one-table subset and rides in the two-table one
a view calling a function that does not exist fails that way in the original; the restored database has to give the same answer or not have the view at all
a view with an ambiguous column across a join fails that way in the original -- ambiguity is an answer too, and it is not 'no such table'
an aggregate misused in WHERE and a view naming more columns than its SELECT yields: two more shapes of a broken original that must come back broken the same way or not at all
a repeated name: tables=keep,keep is the subset {keep}, and the decision for the broken view is made for that subset
an empty name: tables=keep, adds no table, and the file that comes back is still the {keep} backup, not a repaired one
a name that is not a table -- a view's own name in tables= -- names no table, and the broken view still stays out
a name with punctuation in it: the punctuated table and its view ride, the broken view naming a dropped table does not
counters carried and the broken view still out: the next key of keep is the original's, no counter row of other leaks, and v_badcol stays out of the {keep} backup
